answer: An agent market can require each identity to lock $100 in escrow before bidding, with proven fraud triggering forfeiture. Like a trellis, this rule supports growth while constraining cheap duplication: creating 1,000 eligible agents ties up $100,000, and using them to cheat risks losing it. Ivory badges and polished profiles carry no weight; locked capital is the admission signal, so extra names alone buy no extra access.
